evidence: Erasm. Coll., Fōrm. I 68: Valē in crāstinum et tū, mī Petre
terms.comment: In crāstinum, “till tomorrow, for tomorrow”, is classical (vōs vocābō in crāstinum, Plaut. Ps. 5.2.55; in crāstinum differre, Cic. de Or. 2.90.367, Lewis & Short s.v. crāstinus); joined to valē it is the leave-taking of the Renaissance school colloquies. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: Lewis & Short: valeo
Erasmus’s Colloquia quoted from the Latīnitās loci collection, checked against the editions named there.

phrases.latin: Valē, mī Chrīstiāne. — Valē in crāstinum et tū, mī Petre.
phrases.english: Goodbye, Christian. — Goodbye till tomorrow to you too, Peter.
